Forbidden.description: The caller may not perform this operation: the credential is locked or disabled; an IP allowlist set on the organization or the credential refuses the request, or the platform could not read it; the caller's organization is suspended and the request is not a `GET`, `HEAD` or `OPTIONS` request or an export action; the credential lacks a required privilege or may not call this operation; or the caller may not act on the addressed resource. A refusal made before the request is routed has the body `{"error": "forbidden"}`, or `{"error": "organization_suspended"}` when the organization is suspended; a refusal made after routing carries the body of the component that refused it.

NotFound.description: The addressed resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller, or the caller's organization is disabled, being deleted or deleted. A refusal made before the request is routed, for such an organization, has the body `{"error": "organization_unavailable"}`. An unknown path is answered by the router with `{"detail": ...}`; a resource the platform does not find is answered with the body of the component that looked for it.

Unauthorized.description: The API key is missing, invalid, expired or revoked. A refusal made before the request is routed has the body `{"error": "unauthorized"}`; a refusal made after routing carries the body of the component that refused it.

the wire actually carries. It is not the
`{data, page, page_size, total, next}` pagination envelope; no component
between this service and the store applies that envelope, and declaring it here would document a shape
no caller will ever receive.

filter is a property of the (asset, caller) pair rather than a stored column,
so it is applied to each page after the count. When you pass `protection`,
a short or even empty page is ordinary: keep paging while `page` is at most

`ownership` says whether your organization owns this asset (`owned`) or
reaches it through a share (`shared`). `protection` is the asset's
protection class, which governs which generic operations are permitted on
it: `managed` means it belongs to your organization and you may write it;
`platform` means the platform shares it with every organization, and it is
readable and copyable but never writable.

ErrorResponse.description:
Standard error envelope.

Every response this contract declares with this schema uses this shape: validation failures (422), whose field errors are under `details.errors`. Errors raised by route handlers and unhandled exceptions use it too.

It is not the only error shape on the wire. 401, 403 and 404 are declared on the operations that can return them without a body schema, because their bodies differ by producer. Authentication, account-lock and rate-limit refusals may be returned before routing, and 401, 403 or 429 may also be returned with a different body after routing; 404 and 405 from the router use another shape. 429 and 405 are not declared. Do not assume this envelope, or any header set, for a status an operation does not declare with this schema.

A request body over the size limit is refused with 413 by the request-size layer, not by the operation. That response is not this envelope: its body has the keys `error`, `reason` and `limit_bytes`. The default limit is 1 MiB, and `limit_bytes` states the limit that applied. An operation that accepts a larger body states its limit in its description. The signature check on a signed request has its own limit, 1 MiB by default, and its 413 carries `error` and `reason` only. The same layers answer 503 while request-body capacity is in use and 408 when a body is not received in time, each with the keys `error` and `reason`. These refusals carry those bodies even on an operation that declares 413, 503 or 408 with this schema.

service.description: Opaque identifier for the platform component that produced this error. Quote it when reporting a problem; do not branch on its value — it is not part of the stable contract.

Where to fetch the rendered invoice document.

Note: This operation returns a **download location**, not the document bytes.
The rendered invoice is a PDF held in object storage and the API answers
with the URL to retrieve it from; fetch that URL to obtain the file.

The location is **short-lived and single-purpose**: it is minted for the
request that asked for it, expires within the hour, and is not the same
string twice. Fetch it promptly rather than storing it, and ask again
rather than reusing an old one. An invoice that has not been rendered yet

Despite the name, nothing here observes an execution. The validator parses
the script into a syntax tree and inspects it; it does not import, evaluate
or run any part of it, in a sandbox or otherwise. Every field below is a
property of the source **text**, so each is a lower bound: anything a
program assembles at run time is invisible to all three.

Sorted and de-duplicated: a call written once and a call written in a loop both appear once, a call inside an unreachable branch still appears, and no arguments, ordering or counts are reported. The check is a pattern match over string literals, so a URL the script assembles at run time — by concatenation, formatting, an f-string, an environment variable or a configuration value — does not appear here. Use it to notice hard-coded endpoints, not to establish that a component has no egress.

logs.description: Notes from the validator recording which groups of checks it ran. These are the validator's own messages — the script is not run, so it emits nothing. Present only when `validation_profile` is `full`.

ServiceAccountCreate.description:
Body for ``POST /v1/service-accounts``.

Note: ``privileges`` is **capped**, not defaulted: whatever arrives here is
intersected with the creating principal's own grant, so an account cannot be
minted with more privilege than the principal creating it, and asking for
less still works. The same cap applies to ``ServiceAccountUpdate``, so an
account cannot be widened after creation either.

Note: Two states, not three. **Omit** ``privileges`` to inherit your own set;
send a **list** to get a capped subset. An explicit ``null`` is **refused**
(422): on ``PATCH`` a null means "reduce this account to the empty set", and a
created account cannot hold none, so the one reading that would work here is
"everything the creator holds" — the widest possible outcome, spelled the way
a caller spells an empty field. One literal must not mean *empty* on one verb
of this plane and *grant me everything* on the other.

endpoint_access.description: The endpoints the account may call. Omit to give it your own credential's endpoint access; a wider policy, `null` included, is refused with `403`.

expires_at.description: When the credential stops authenticating, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. Omit for a credential that does not expire.
expires_at.title: Expires At

name.description: A display name for the account. Omit for a default name.
name.title: Name

privileges.description: The privileges the account holds. Omit to give it the privileges your own credential holds, or send a list to request a subset of them; `null` is refused with `422`.
privileges.title: Privileges

ServiceAccountCreate.title: ServiceAccountCreate

ServiceAccountCreated.description: The creation response — the only body that ever carries key material.

key.description: Full plaintext key. Returned once, on creation, never again.
key.title: Key

ServiceAccountCreated.title: ServiceAccountCreated

ServiceAccountRead.description:
A service account as every READ path returns it.

Note: There is no ``key`` field and there must never be one: key material is
returned exactly once, on creation, and no read path may return it
again.

``prefix`` is a display label shared by every key in the organization. It
does not identify a single key and does not change on rotation; identify an
account by ``id``. Identifiers, ``prefix`` included, are opaque and MUST NOT
be parsed by clients.
ServiceAccountRead.title: ServiceAccountRead

ServiceAccountRevoked.description: The body ``DELETE /v1/service-accounts/{id}`` returns on a successful revoke.
ServiceAccountRevoked.title: ServiceAccountRevoked

ServiceAccountUpdate.description:
Body for ``PATCH /v1/service-accounts/{service_account_id}``.

Note: ``privileges`` is **capped** exactly as on create — intersected with the
editing principal's own grant — so this operation cannot widen an account
beyond its editor. Omit the field to leave privileges untouched, or send a
list to set a capped subset. Omitting the field is not the same as sending an
empty list.

Note: ``null`` and ``[]`` both mean the empty set, and an empty set is
**refused** with 422 ("privileges list must not be empty"). Sending either
does not leave the account holding nothing — no request on this route can.

endpoint_access.description: A new endpoint access policy, replacing the current one. Omit to leave it unchanged.

expires_at.description: A new expiry, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. Omit to leave the current expiry unchanged.
expires_at.title: Expires At

is_active.description: Not applied: sending it changes nothing. To stop an account authenticating, revoke it with `DELETE /v1/service-accounts/{service_account_id}`.
is_active.title: Is Active

name.description: A new display name for the account.
name.title: Name

privileges.description: The account's new privilege set, capped to the privileges your own credential holds. Omit to leave the account's privileges unchanged; `null` and `[]` are refused with `422`.
privileges.title: Privileges

ServiceAccountUpdate.title: ServiceAccountUpdate

Evaluate a rule against a synthetic event and report what would happen. A rule that does not exist and one belonging to another organization both return `404`.

The body is optional: send nothing to test against a default event, or supply any of `event_type`, `message` and `source_name` to shape it.

**This really delivers.** When the rule matches, the notification is sent to the rule's configured channels and real recipients receive it. `dispatched` reports whether that happened and `recipients` how many people it reached.

post.description:
Create an asset in your organization from a bundle previously produced by `GET /v1/assets/{asset_id}/export`.

The bundle's `export_type` selects what is created — a component, an orchestration or an intelligence — and the response shape follows from it.

The asset is created in your own organization and is attributed to the credential you present. If your credential reaches more than one organization you must name the destination in `organization_id`, and it must be one of yours; a destination outside them is refused. Any organization named inside the bundle itself is ignored, and a bundle whose `export_type` is not recognised is rejected.

The request-size limit is 16 MiB: a larger request body is refused with `413`.

**Access.** The privileges checked follow the bundle's `export_type`; every one listed for that type is required:

- `component`: `COMPONENT_CREATE`
- `orchestration`: `ORCHESTRATION_CREATE`, `COMPONENT_CREATE`
- `intelligence`: `INTELLIGENCE_CREATE`, `COMPONENT_CREATE`
- `program`: `PROGRAM_CREATE`

201.description: The asset was created. The body's shape follows the bundle type.

400.description: Unrecognised bundle, or the destination organization is ambiguous

413.description: The request body is larger than the request-size limit. The body has the keys `error`, `reason` and `limit_bytes`.

422.description: Validation failed. Field errors are under `details.errors`.

post.description:
Copy any asset you can read into a writable asset of your own, with a new identifier.

This is how you adopt a platform template: a shared, read-only master becomes an ordinary asset in your organization that you can then update and run. The copy is attributed to the credential you present, and its name defaults to the source name followed by `(copy)`.

The copy is created in your own organization. If your credential reaches more than one you must name the destination in `organization_id`, and it must be one of yours; a destination outside them is refused. An identifier belonging to another organization is answered `404`, the same as one that does not exist. A copy starts a new lineage: it does not inherit the source's version history.

**Access.** The privileges checked follow the asset's own type. Copying a source in one of your own organizations requires the type's read and create privileges on it, and every copy requires the type's create privilege in the destination organization. Copying a platform template (a shared, read-only master) requires only the create privilege in the destination organization. Either requirement unmet is answered `403`:

- `orchestration_component`: `COMPONENT_READ` and `COMPONENT_CREATE`
- `intelligence_component`: `COMPONENT_READ` and `COMPONENT_CREATE`
- `orchestration`: `ORCHESTRATION_READ` and `ORCHESTRATION_CREATE`
- `program`: `PROGRAM_READ` and `PROGRAM_CREATE`
- `secret`: `SECRET_READ` and `SECRET_CREATE`
- `intelligence`: `INTELLIGENCE_READ` and `INTELLIGENCE_CREATE`

post.description:
Grant a user individual privileges on an asset, overriding whatever they would inherit from group membership.

Granting the same user again replaces their previous grant rather than adding to it.

Only the asset's owner or an administrator of its subscription may grant access; any other caller in the same organization is answered `403`. An asset belonging to another organization is answered `404`. The grant is recorded in the compliance audit trail against the credential you presented — it cannot be attributed to anyone else.

`user_id` must name a **user profile**. The identity `GET /v1/whoami` returns for an API key is the API key's id, not a user profile id, and is refused here with `400`. Both are UUIDs, so they parse identically and the refusal arrives only when the grant is attempted.

**Access.** Besides being the asset's owner or an administrator, the caller needs the share privilege for the asset's type on its organization:

- `orchestration_component`: `COMPONENT_SHARE`
- `intelligence_component`: `COMPONENT_SHARE`
- `orchestration`: `ORCHESTRATION_SHARE`
- `program`: no share privilege
- `secret`: no share privilege
- `intelligence`: no share privilege

A caller who is not an administrator must also hold every privilege the request adds or removes, on the asset or its organization. Either requirement unmet is answered `403`.

Address the grant by the `user_id` on the grant record, not by its `id` field.

Only the asset's owner or an administrator of its subscription may revoke access; any other caller in the same organization is answered `403`. An asset belonging to another organization is answered `404`, as is a grant that does not exist or was already revoked.

**Access.** Besides being the asset's owner or an administrator, the caller needs the share privilege for the asset's type on its organization:

- `orchestration_component`: `COMPONENT_SHARE`
- `intelligence_component`: `COMPONENT_SHARE`
- `orchestration`: `ORCHESTRATION_SHARE`
- `program`: no share privilege
- `secret`: no share privilege
- `intelligence`: no share privilege

A caller who is not an administrator must also hold every privilege the request adds or removes, on the asset or its organization. Either requirement unmet is answered `403`.

post.description:
Grant a role, or direct privileges, to a user, group or service account on a resource of your organization.

An API key needs `GRANT_CREATE` on its organization. A credential grants only what it holds: an API key must itself hold, on the resource, every privilege the grant confers, and is answered `403` otherwise. Its privileges are its own; the person who created the key is recorded as the granter and lends it no authority. The role must be a platform system role or one of your organization's roles. The grantee must belong to the resource's organization; a user who receives an organization grant must already be an active member. Either refusal is `403`.

Only your own organization's resources and grants are reachable. A resource, role or grant that does not exist, has been revoked, or belongs to another organization is answered `404`; these are indistinguishable by design.

A second grant to the same grantee on the same resource is answered `409`; change the existing grant instead. On an asset or capability built from other assets, a change that would leave the grantee holding a privilege on the composite but not on what it is built from is refused with `409`: the body carries `change_set`, and `reason` is `requires_confirmation` (preview then apply it) or `refused` (it reaches assets you do not administer). To apply the whole set as one change, send the same grant to `POST /v1/grants/preview` and then `POST /v1/grants/apply`: `role_id` for a role, or `privileges` for direct privileges.

Grants are reversible with `DELETE /v1/grants/{grant_id}`. A grant on a group is not available here and is answered `422`. `401` is answered without a valid credential.

post.description:
Apply a previewed change set. The set is recomputed rather than taken from the request; when its fingerprint still matches and nothing is blocked, every row is written in one transaction.

Send exactly one of `privilege` (one privilege; the only form a revoke takes), `privileges` (several privileges written as one direct grant) and `role_id` (a role). `replaces_grant_id` names the grantee's existing grant on this resource, which is ended in the same change; it is valid on a grant in the `privileges` or `role_id` form only. A body breaking these rules is answered `422`. Send the body you previewed, plus its `fingerprint` and an optional `reason`, which is recorded on every grant the change ends.

`grant_ids` lists every grant written, the replaced grant first; `revoked_grant_ids` names the grants ended.

An API key needs `GRANT_CREATE` for a grant, `GRANT_REVOKE` for a revoke, and both for a grant with `replaces_grant_id`, because the replaced grant is ended. It must be allowed to manage grants on the resource and, for a grant, hold every privilege conferred; with `replaces_grant_id`, also every privilege the replaced grant confers. Otherwise the answer is `403`. The person who created the key lends it no authority. `404` is answered for a resource that is absent or not visible to you, for a `role_id` that is deleted or another organization's (before any `403`), and for a `replaces_grant_id` that is not the grantee's own live grant on this resource, with the same answer an unknown id gets.

`409` is answered, and nothing is written, when the set has moved since the preview (`reason` `stale`, a stale preview, with the fresh `change_set` to confirm again; a role edited in between, or a replaced grant no longer live, is stale too) or cannot be applied (`reason` `refused`). A repeat after success is answered `409`, because the set has moved. `401` is answered without a valid credential.

post.description: Chunk, embed and index documents into a search-index index. Any of `text_field`, `vector_field` and `embedding_model` that is omitted is auto-detected from the index mapping. Accepts up to 10 files per request, each at most 10 MiB. The request-size limit is 105,906,176 bytes, which is 10 files of that size plus 1 MiB for the form: a larger request body is refused with `413`. Send up to 10 files of at most 10 MiB each, with extensions .csv, .json, .jsonl, .md, .txt. A request without a `Content-Length` (including a chunked one) is refused with 411, and one whose declared length or any file exceeds the limit with 413, before any file is sent on. A body that is not `multipart/form-data` is refused with 415, and a `Content-Length` that is not a number with 400. An unsupported file, too many files, or a field that cannot be detected answers 400. A key without `INFRA_CONFIGURE` is refused with 403 before the body is read. Files are forwarded one at a time within a whole-request time budget: a file not reached before the budget is exhausted is reported in its `files` entry with status `not_attempted` and nothing is written for it, and a forward that times out -- at the gateway or at this service -- is reported with status `timeout`, meaning the ingest may still complete, so read the store back before re-sending; both are reported inside a 200 and neither counts toward the returned totals. A name that is not a single path segment answers 404. Unless `text_field`, `vector_field` and `embedding_model` are all sent, the index is read first, before any file is sent, and a refusal of that read is the answer: an unknown index answers 404. A 409 means your organization's search index is not running, so nothing was done. A 503 means the platform could not get an answer from your organization's search index, or could not complete the request. Any other error the search index answers is relayed with its own status, for example 429 when it is too busy to take the request. A 502 means the platform could not reach the store, or the store answered with an error. When all three are sent, nothing is read first, and a refusal of a file, including one because your organization's search index is not running, is reported in that file's `files` entry, with a 200. A file whose forward times out, or that the request time budget did not reach, is reported the same way -- as that file's `timeout` or `not_attempted` entry -- rather than failing the batch.

post.description: Chunk, embed and insert documents into a vector-store collection. Any of `text_field`, `vector_field` and `embedding_model` that is omitted is auto-detected from the collection's schema. Accepts up to 10 files per request, each at most 10 MiB. The request-size limit is 105,906,176 bytes, which is 10 files of that size plus 1 MiB for the form: a larger request body is refused with `413`. Send up to 10 files of at most 10 MiB each, with extensions .csv, .json, .jsonl, .md, .txt. A request without a `Content-Length` (including a chunked one) is refused with 411, and one whose declared length or any file exceeds the limit with 413, before any file is sent on. A body that is not `multipart/form-data` is refused with 415, and a `Content-Length` that is not a number with 400. An unsupported file, too many files, or a field that cannot be detected answers 400. A key without `INFRA_CONFIGURE` is refused with 403 before the body is read. Files are forwarded one at a time within a whole-request time budget: a file not reached before the budget is exhausted is reported in its `files` entry with status `not_attempted` and nothing is written for it, and a forward that times out -- at the gateway or at this service -- is reported with status `timeout`, meaning the ingest may still complete, so read the store back before re-sending; both are reported inside a 200 and neither counts toward the returned totals. A name that is not a single path segment answers 404. Unless `text_field`, `vector_field` and `embedding_model` are all sent, the collection is read first, before any file is sent, and a refusal of that read is the answer: an unknown collection answers 404. A 409 means your organization's vector store is not running, so nothing was done. A 503 means the platform could not get an answer from your organization's vector store, or could not complete the request. A 502 means the platform could not reach the store, or the store answered with an error. When all three are sent, nothing is read first, and a refusal of a file, including one because your organization's vector store is not running, is reported in that file's `files` entry, with a 200. A file whose forward times out, or that the request time budget did not reach, is reported the same way -- as that file's `timeout` or `not_attempted` entry -- rather than failing the batch.

get.description:
One query grammar over the platform's logs: a run's recorded lines, an orchestration's, an intelligence's, a capability's, and the organization's own.

**Selectors.** `scope` is `run`, `orchestration`, `intelligence`, `capability` or `organization`; `component` is recognised but has no log channels and returns `422`. `scope_id` identifies the scoped resource and is required for every scope except `organization`, which is always the organization the calling key belongs to.

**Channels.** For `scope=run`, `channel` is one recorded log type (`provider`, `conversation`, `conversation_input`, `conversation_stream`, `error`, `extension`, `snapshot` or `state_transition`); omitted, every type is returned. An orchestration serves `provider`, `conversation`, `error`, `state`, `extension` and `snapshot`; an intelligence `error` and `extension`; a capability `system`, `error`, `extension` and `snapshot`; the organization `system`, `error`, `extension` and `notification`. For every scope except `run`, an omitted `channel` reads `error`.

**Parameters.** `from` and `to` bound the window (an RFC 3339 time; a run also accepts unix nanoseconds) and `limit` caps the page, up to 5000 for a run, 10000 for an orchestration, 500 for notifications and 1000 otherwise. `q` searches the lines of an intelligence, a capability or the organization. `version` pins an exact semantic version of an intelligence or a capability; `service_type` narrows an intelligence's lines, and `level` its extension lines. Notifications also take `domain`, `severity` and `offset`. A run's lines are returned `newest_first` (the default) or `oldest_first` (`order`), and are always confined to the run's own start and end: a bound outside them is narrowed to them, and a run that has not started returns an empty page.

**Refusals.** A selector value, combination or parameter that is not served for the scope returns `422` naming what is. So does `organization_id`: the organization always comes from the credential.

**API keys, `scope=intelligence`.** `INTELLIGENCE_VIEW_LOGS` on an intelligence is derived from the key: it must hold `READ`, `INTELLIGENCE_READ`, `WRITE`, `EXECUTE`, `INTELLIGENCE_TRAIN`, `MANAGE` or `ADMIN`, or have a direct grant on the intelligence. A run, orchestration, intelligence or capability in another organization, or one the caller may not read, is answered `404`.

post.description:
Invite a person to join your organization by e-mail.

The person becomes a member only when they accept. The invitation expires after the platform's invitation period, 7 days unless your platform operator has changed it, and a resend starts that period again. There is no way to add an existing account directly through this API. The answer is the new invitation, which you can resend or cancel through the invitation operations.

The organization is taken from the credential you present, never from the request, so this operation cannot be pointed at another organization.

An API key needs `ORG_MANAGE_MEMBERS`; without it the answer is `403`. A key can only hand out what it holds itself: it must hold every privilege of the role it invites the person into, otherwise the answer is `403`. `role` is one of `admin`, `billing_admin` and `member`; `global_admin` cannot be conferred through this API.

An invitation that collides with an existing one is answered `409`, and its `detail` says which: `code` is `already_a_member` when the address already belongs to a member, and `invitation_pending` when an invitation to it is still pending, with that invitation's `invitation_id` so you can resend it instead. `401` is answered without a valid credential.

delete.description:
Remove a member from your organization.

The member's access to your organization's resources is revoked and the membership is kept as removed, so it can be restored; revoked access is not given back by a restore. A member who owns groups cannot be removed until you name, in `handoff_to_user_id`, an active administrator to take those groups over: without one the answer is `409` with `handoff_required`, and naming the member being removed, or someone who is not an active administrator, is answered `400`. A successful removal answers `204`, and repeating it answers `404`.

The organization is taken from the credential you present, never from the request, so this operation cannot be pointed at another organization. A user who is not a member of your organization is answered `404`, whether or not the user exists.

An API key needs `ORG_MANAGE_MEMBERS`; without it the answer is `403`. A key can only hand out what it holds itself: it must hold every privilege of the member's role, otherwise the answer is `403`. A member whose role is `global_admin` is never a key's to remove; that is answered `403` with `global_admin_reserved`.

A change that would leave your organization without an active administrator, or without an active `global_admin`, is refused with `409`. `401` is answered without a valid credential.

get.description:
One query grammar over the platform's operational metrics: run statistics for a capability or an orchestration, and service metrics for an intelligence.

**Selectors.** `subject` is `capability`, `orchestration` or `intelligence`; `component` and `service` are recognised but not yet reportable and return `422`. `subject_id` is the subject's identifier. Without `series` the subject's summary is returned. `series=runs` returns run counts bucketed over time for a capability or an orchestration. For an intelligence, `series` names one metric (`latency_p50`, `latency_p95`, `latency_p99`, `throughput`, `accuracy`, `drift_score` or `error_rate`) and returns it as a time series.

**Window.** `window` is a lookback preset (`1h`, `6h`, `24h`, `7d`, `30d`). An intelligence series defaults to `24h`; every other form uses the subject's own default when `window` is omitted. `from` and `to` are not accepted: a window must be one of the presets.

**Series options.** `granularity` (`1m`, `5m`, `1h`, `1d`) and `model_id` apply only to an intelligence series. `granularity` defaults to a bucket size suited to the window. `model_id` narrows the prediction-derived metrics to one model. `version` pins an exact semantic version of the subject; omitted, the report covers every version.

**Refusals.** Any selector value or combination that is not served returns `422` naming the values that are. So do `metric`, `from`, `to` and `organization_id`: the organization always comes from the credential.

**Privileges** depend on the selectors (`x-perceivo-privilege-by`): `INTELLIGENCE_READ` on the capability; `ORCHESTRATION_READ` on the orchestration; `INTELLIGENCE_READ` on the intelligence for its summary, and `INTELLIGENCE_READ` plus `INTELLIGENCE_LIST` on the intelligence for a series. A subject in another organization is answered `404`.

post.description:
Create the next version of the orchestration this draft is bound to (the draft's `base_version_id`), applying the draft's `publish_payload` — `patch`, `secret_ops` and `change_note` — and its `staged_changes`, in one step. On success the draft is deleted and the response names the new version's `orchestration_id`. On any failure nothing is created and the draft is kept.

This is how an orchestration's graph (`nodes`, `ports`, `edges`, `secrets`) and runtime settings (`capability_image_id`, `additional_packages`, `requires_gpu`, `runtime_config`) are changed: save them in the draft with `PATCH /v1/orchestrations/drafts/{draft_id}`, then publish.

Requires the `ORCHESTRATION_CREATE_VERSION` privilege on the draft's base version.

Send the draft's `base_version_id` as `expected_base_version_id`.

Refusals:

- `409` `DRAFT_BASE_STALE` — the base is no longer the orchestration's latest version, or `expected_base_version_id` is not the draft's base. Start a new draft from the latest version.
- `409` `LINEAGE_VERSION_CONFLICT` — another version was created at the same moment. Retry.
- `409` `DRAFT_NOT_LINEAGE_BOUND` — the draft is not bound to a published version.
- `409` `DRAFT_PAYLOAD_MISSING` — the draft has no `publish_payload`.
- `422` `ORCHESTRATION_INVALID` — the resulting orchestration fails validation.
- `422` `STAGED_CHANGE_TARGET_MISSING` — a staged change names a node the new version does not have.

Requires the `ORCHESTRATION_EXECUTE` privilege. Starts a run of this orchestration. Put the run's input under `input` (or `input_data`) in the body; other top-level keys are not read by the run.

To review a blocking human-review node of this run yourself, name it in `reviewer_assignments` by `node_id`. The assignee is always the calling API key; naming another subject, a group, or a type other than `USER` is refused with `422` and no run is started.

**The response identifies the work in one of two ways and a caller must handle both.** `result.run_id` is a run that exists and is readable with `GET /v1/orchestrations/runs/{run_id}`. `result.request_id`, with `result.run_id` null, is an input accepted onto the capability's queue for which no run exists yet.

Which one you get is decided server-side by the capability behind the orchestration; it is not a property of the request. A standalone orchestration, an experimental capability, and a capability with no active traffic plan always return `run_id`. A capability whose execution mode is `persistent` returns `run_id` when a replica is free at that instant and `request_id` when none is, so two identical calls seconds apart can differ. An `on_demand` capability always returns `request_id`.

On the queued paths, resolve the `request_id` with `GET /v1/queue?kind=input&asset_id={capability_id}`: it returns each queued, running and recent input carrying both its `id` and its `run_id`, so match on `id == request_id`. That lookup is keyed by **capability**, and neither this response nor `GET /v1/orchestrations/{orchestration_id}` carries the orchestration's `capability_id` — so you must already know which capability you invoked. Supplying `callback_url` in the body avoids the lookup entirely. Calling `GET /v1/orchestrations/runs/{run_id}` with a null, or with a request id, returns `404`.

delete.description:
Cancel a review that is no longer needed.

Note: **The review is cancelled, not deleted.** It moves to a cancelled status and remains readable through `GET /v1/reviews` and `GET /v1/reviews/{review_id}`. Nothing is removed.

Only a pending or in-progress review can be cancelled; one that has already reached a final status is refused `409`.

Note: Cancelling a **blocking** review does not resume the run it parked. A run waiting on a review that is cancelled stays parked.

Note: **Visibility is checked first, and separately from authority.** A review you cannot see is answered `404` — not `403` — before this operation's authority check is reached, so a refusal does not tell you which of the two stopped you. You can see a review when you own it — you are its assignee, its creator or its completer — when you are a member of the group it is assigned to, when you have read access to the orchestration it belongs to, when you hold `REVIEW_ADMIN` on the organization, or when you administer the organization. Seeing a review never confers the right to change it.

Requires control of the reviewed asset — `ORCHESTRATION_EXECUTE` on the linked orchestration, or `CAPABILITY_INVOKE` on the linked capability — or the `REVIEW_ADMIN` or `REVIEW_CANCEL` privilege on the organization.

Note: **`PATCH` and `DELETE` on a review apply the same gate**, so any grant that admits one admits the other. A principal you allow to cancel a review can also reassign it, which returns it to pending and discards an in-progress reviewer's claim.

Note: A caller with no user profile — the ordinary case for an API key — is admitted by organization administration **alone**: the privilege and asset-control routes above are not consulted for it. Conversely, organization administration is not an alternative route for a caller that does have a profile — for that caller only the asset-control and privilege routes above apply. (Record visibility is checked separately and does admit organization administration in both cases.)

**This is how a service account becomes able to complete a review.** Only the assignee may complete one, and an API key is never an assignee by default: reviews are raised by the platform when a run reaches a review gate and are assigned from the run's configured reviewers, which never name a key. Claiming assigns the review to the calling credential; it takes no subject, and cannot be used to assign to anyone else.

Requires the `REVIEW_PERFORM` privilege.

post.description:
Create a service account.

Note: The response is the ONLY body that ever carries key material. No read path
returns it again.

Important: ``privileges`` is **capped, not defaulted**: the set you send is
intersected with the privileges your own credential **effectively** holds on
this organization — including the ones it holds through a role — so a service
account can never be created with more privilege than its creator. Asking for
**less** works and is the intended use: mint each account least-privilege.
Omitting the field gives the account your own set.

Note: A request naming **only** privileges you do not hold is refused with
``403``, naming them. A request naming **some** that you hold is created
holding just those. Neither is a schema error, so neither answers ``422``.

Note: ``endpoint_access`` and ``allowed_ips`` are confined the same way.
**Omitting** either gives the new account your own credential's value, so an
account you mint is never reachable from more addresses, or against more
endpoint groups, than the credential that minted it. Asking for anything
wider — an explicit ``null`` included — is refused with ``403`` naming the
field.

Note: Sending ``privileges: null`` is **refused with 422**. An account cannot be created
holding no privileges, so the only reading a null could have here is "give me
everything you hold" — the widest outcome, spelled the way an empty field is
spelled. Omit the field if that is what you want. On
``PATCH /v1/service-accounts/{id}`` the same literal means "reduce this
account to the empty set", and one literal must not mean *empty* on one verb
of a plane and *grant me everything* on the other.

The same privilege cap applies to ``PATCH /v1/service-accounts/{id}``, so an
account cannot be widened after creation either.

`privileges` is **capped** here exactly as it is on create: whatever you send is intersected with the set your own credential holds, so this operation cannot widen an account beyond its editor. Narrowing works.

post.description:
Run this trigger's orchestration immediately, without waiting for its schedule.

The run starts asynchronously, and the response is `202` with an OperationEnvelope. Note: the run's status cannot currently be looked up through the public API; the `poll` URL in the response, which `Location` repeats, does not resolve.

Supply `input_payload` to override the input for this one run. Omit it and the trigger's stored input is used; either way the stored value is left unchanged.

Invoking a trigger does not disturb its schedule — the next scheduled run still happens when it was going to, and this run is not recorded as the trigger's last scheduled firing.

A trigger belonging to another organization answers `404`, the same `404` as one that does not exist or has been deleted. Answers `502` when the run could not be started, in which case nothing was started and it is safe to retry.

One query grammar over the organization's cost and consumption reports.

`group_by` selects the aggregation dimension; omitting it returns the organization-wide report. **Six dimensions are served** — `capability`, `component`, `orchestration`, `intelligence`, `experiment`, `infrastructure`. `service` and `day` are recognised but not yet reportable and return `422` naming the dimensions that are, rather than answering with a different report.

`format=csv` is available only for the ungrouped organization report. A `csv` request combined with a `group_by` is refused rather than silently answered as JSON.

`from` and `to` bound the reporting window. They are **required for the ungrouped organization report and its CSV form**, which serve no unbounded result; a request for either without them is refused with a `422`. Every `group_by` form treats them as optional filters and returns the full history when they are omitted.

This condition cannot be expressed in OpenAPI, which can mark a parameter required or optional but not required-when-another-is-absent. The parameters are therefore published as optional and the rule stated here.

get.description:
List the event types a webhook may subscribe to now, with the JSON Schema of the `data` object each one delivers. Use it to choose a webhook's `events` before calling `POST /v1/webhooks` or `PATCH /v1/webhooks/{webhook_id}`: those operations accept exactly the types this list returns, and refuse any other with `400`. The list is the same for every organization and changes only when the platform starts or stops emitting a type, so it is safe to cache. This operation reads nothing and changes nothing; it takes no parameters, and repeating it is harmless.

**Authorization:** any authenticated caller. No named privilege is required. A key restricted to endpoint groups needs the `webhooks` group.

**Response:** a JSON array, one object per event type, in a stable order. `name` is the value to put in `events` and the `event_type` of each delivery; `version` is the version of the `data` object; `description` says what happened; `data` is the JSON Schema of the delivery's `data` object. Today the list has one entry, `review.completed` at `version` 1, whose `data` schema requires `organization_id`, `severity`, `title` and `target`.

**Errors:** `401` when the request carries no valid API key. `403` when the key is restricted to endpoint groups that do not include `webhooks`. `429` when requests arrive too fast; wait for the `Retry-After` seconds. `502` when the platform could not produce the list; retry with backoff.

**Example:** `curl -H "X-API-Key: $PERCEIVO_API_KEY" https://api.perceivo.ai/v1/webhooks/event-types`

**Related:** `POST /v1/webhooks` to subscribe, and `PATCH /v1/webhooks/{webhook_id}` to change a subscription.

502.description: The platform could not produce the list: `upstream_unavailable` when the backing service did not answer with the list, `upstream_contract_violation` when it answered with something that is not a list of event types. Retry with backoff.
